page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-8 is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 Intel Xeon platform running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, backed by 33 MB of L3 cache. System memory is configured at 8.0 GB of RAM, yielding a 1.0 GB per vCPU allocation ratio. This instance includes hardware support for vector processing with AVX-512 extensions and AES cryptographic execution, but contains no discrete GPUs or attached local NVMe storage.

Synthetic benchmark evaluation indicates moderate multi-core performance alongside lower single-core execution speed. While single-threaded scores in stress-ng and Geekbench fall into lower performance brackets, multi-threaded execution demonstrates solid scaling, reaching a PassMark CPU score of 8305.34 and a Redis throughput of 7.13 million SET operations per second. Memory bandwidth reaches 48.32 GB/s for large uncached block reads, providing sufficient throughput for network-oriented applications.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, n2-highcpu-8 delivers core density for CPU-bound tasks that do not require substantial memory overhead. The primary hardware tradeoff is the limited 1 GB RAM per vCPU memory capacity, which precludes running large in-memory databases or memory-heavy data processing pipelines. Optimal workload fits include stateless web servers, microservices, CI/CD build environments, software compilation, and small-model inference processing.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-8 is a compute-optimized virtual machine powered by a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon x86_64 processor. The configuration delivers 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores with hyper-threading and 33 MB of L3 cache, paired with 8.0 GB of system memory. Hardware feature support includes AVX-512 and AES instructions, though the instance lacks local NVMe storage and discrete GPUs. In performance benchmarks, the server demonstrates average multi-core CPU and memory bandwidth performance, achieving 7.13 million Redis SET operations per second and 6.62 GB/s in static web serving tests. Single-core processing throughput remains lower. Designed for compute-heavy tasks that do not demand extensive memory, n2-highcpu-8 offers core-dense allocation efficiency. The key tradeoff is the strict 1 GB per vCPU memory capacity, making it best suited for lightweight web serving, CI/CD code compilation, network microservices, and small-model inference tasks.
